area: Event Groups list/detail plus legacy Projects pages

screens.name: Event Groups list
screens.purpose: Read-only worklist of Event Groups (shared grouping context across independent incidents) that lets operational staff find a group by title/location and open its record.
roles: Gate: RoleRoute roles={OPERATIONAL_ROLE_NAMES} (web/src/App.tsx:61-68; web/src/utils/roleModel.ts:17-24). Maintenance field workers are redirected to /submissions (web/src/auth/RoleRoute.tsx:19). Sidebar entry only when isOperationalUser (web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:85).
primaryTasks: Find a specific Event Group by title, county, route or description
Scan open groups for incident volume and recency to decide where to look next

responsive.layout: AppShell (sidebar becomes a stacked 'Navigation' card below lg) → single column: flex-wrap toolbar, optional error banner, one 6-column table inside an overflow-x-auto rounded panel.
breakpointsUsed: overflow-x-auto on table wrapper, w-full table (EventGroupsPage.tsx:78-79)
Shell: lg:flex-row sidebar, lg:hidden mobile nav card, md:px-6 (AppShell.tsx:163-165)
phoneRisks: 375px: the 6-column table cannot fit; the wrapper scrolls horizontally with no sticky first column, so title and Action are never visible together (EventGroupsPage.tsx:78-80).
Toolbar wraps into 3-4 rows (search full width, then select, summary text, Refresh) pushing the table below the fold (EventGroupsPage.tsx:64-74).
'Open Event Group' chip is text-[11px] px-2 py-1 (~22px tall) — well under a 44px touch target (EventGroupsPage.tsx:91).
Title is a Link styled text-[var(--ink)] with hover-only colour change; on touch there is no visible cue that it is tappable (EventGroupsPage.tsx:86).
Mobile nav card is rendered above the content, so the user scrolls past the whole navigation list before reaching the toolbar (AppShell.tsx:164).
tabletRisks: 768-1024px: sidebar is still the stacked mobile card (lg breakpoint is 1024), consuming ~300px of vertical space above the list (AppShell.tsx:164-165).
Table generally fits at 768px but title/location cells wrap onto 2-3 lines; row hover highlight is hover-only (EventGroupsPage.tsx:85).
desktopNotes: At lg+ the sidebar is 256px (collapsible to 64px) and content is capped at max-w-[1900px]; the table stretches to full width with no max width, so on wide monitors the six columns are separated by large whitespace (AppShell.tsx:163-165; EventGroupsPage.tsx:79).
Summary counts render as xs muted text inline in the toolbar — easy to miss compared with the KPI cards the legacy Projects page used (EventGroupsPage.tsx:72).

painPoints.issue: Hard-coded limit=500 with no pagination, sorting or truncation notice; the summary counts silently describe only the first 500 groups.
Duplicate affordance: title link and 'Open Event Group' chip go to the same place, costing a column and horizontal scroll on phones.
Search is scoped to the current status filter (default OPEN); searching for a closed group returns 'No Event Groups match the current filters' without suggesting the filter be widened.
Search input and status select have no label or aria-label; the placeholder is the only label.
Error banner is not role=alert while the detail page's integrity banner is; screen-reader users are not told the load failed.
Link affordance relies on hover colour only; title links are the same colour as body text.
Vocabulary drift inside one row: status 'Open' (group) vs 'active' (open_incident_count) vs 'Last activity'.
Status badge component lives in a page module and is imported by another page instead of features/eventGroups or ui.

strengths: Single compact table with the same column grammar as Incidents/Assessments; header styling (11px uppercase tracking) consistent across the redesign (EventGroupsPage.tsx:80).
Sensible default (OPEN) plus a four-option filter that covers the whole lifecycle including ARCHIVED (EventGroupsPage.tsx:66-71).
Debounced server search with explicit 'Refreshing…' state and distinct loading vs empty messaging (EventGroupsPage.tsx:49-53,73,83).
Uses <Link> for navigation (right-click / open in new tab works), unlike the legacy Projects page (EventGroupsPage.tsx:86,91).
Shared eventGroupLocationLabel and status label helpers keep location/status text identical across list, detail and Mission Center (eventGroupTypes.ts:71-85).
Table is wrapped in overflow-x-auto so the page body never scrolls horizontally (EventGroupsPage.tsx:78).

screens.name: Event Group detail
screens.purpose: Read-only record of one Event Group showing its header facts, the incidents grouped under it with cross-links, and the audited group history.
roles: Same as list: OPERATIONAL_ROLE_NAMES via RoleRoute (web/src/App.tsx:69-76); others redirected to /submissions (web/src/auth/RoleRoute.tsx:19).
No role-conditional UI inside the page — every reaching role sees identical content and links (no edit/close/reopen controls exist).
primaryTasks: Understand what the group is (title, location, status, volume, recency)
See which incidents belong to it and their status/stage, then jump to an incident, its assessment/submission, or the Mission Center map
Review the group's history (who did what, when)

overflow-x-auto incidents table, whitespace-nowrap on Status and Links cells (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:110,126-127)

phoneRisks: 375px: 4-column incidents table with nowrap Status ('In progress · Awaiting Assessment') and nowrap Links cell forces horizontal scroll; the incident title is off-screen while tapping chips (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:111-134).
Chips are text-[11px] px-2 py-1 (~22px tall) and several can wrap into a cluster; small, adjacent touch targets (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:129-131).

Header dl (Incidents/Created/Last activity) wraps under the title as a 2-column grid — works, but 'shrink-0' means a long title block can push it below rather than compress (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:88-96).

tabletRisks: 768-1279px: incidents and history stack (xl breakpoint), so the history sits below a potentially long incidents table; no jump link (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:107).

desktopNotes: At xl+ the incidents/history split works well; history is capped at 520px with its own scroll (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:107,144).
Header card uses a compact dl with justify-between — reads as a proper record header at desktop widths (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:86-99).

painPoints.issue: Page fetches the entire assessments list (limit 1000) in parallel with the group just to map incident→assessment links; render waits for both, and incidents whose assessment is outside the first 1000 silently lose their Assessment/Submission chips.
incidentStatusText maps every status except RESOLVED / IN_PROGRESS to 'New', so any other backend status is mislabeled.
Cross-links are labeled only by numeric ids ('Assessment #12', 'Submission #34'); no state or date, so users cannot tell which chip is the current one.
Two different targets for 'incident' links on the same page: table title → /incidents/:id, history 'Incident #N' → Mission Center map.

No lifecycle or edit actions on the record (read-only by design per AppShell IA comment); the legacy Project detail had Close/Reopen/Edit, so coordinators lose an obvious place to close a group unless My Work covers it.
Load error banner lacks role=alert while the integrity banner has it; inconsistent announcement.
Closed groups show no closed_at / closed-by information even though the API returns it.
Broken-row tint uses an inline style with a hard-coded color-mix instead of a token class, diverging from the rest of the design system.
No breadcrumb; h1 is the group title alone, so the record type is only inferable from the '#id' sub-line and the sidebar highlight.
Table has no sort or filter; large groups list incidents in API order with no way to surface active ones first.

strengths: Compact single header card with a dl of the three facts that matter (incidents, created, last activity) — denser and calmer than the legacy five-card grid (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:86-99).
Data-integrity guard: incidents without a permanent key are flagged at page level (role=alert) and per row, with plain-language explanation (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:70,101-105,123).
Rich, consistent cross-linking to Mission Center, incident, assessment and submission records using one chip style (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:129-131).
Two-column xl layout with a bounded, scrollable history keeps the incidents table primary (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:107,144).
Reuses EventGroupStatusBadge and eventGroupLocationLabel so list and detail read identically (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:7,10).
Uses <Link> everywhere; 'View on Mission Center map' and per-incident 'Map' preserve the group/incident context in the URL (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:78,129).

Optional lifecycle note captured with the action, feeding the audited history (ProjectManagementPanel.tsx:166-169).
State-appropriate button set (only Close for OPEN, only Reopen for CLOSED, nothing for ARCHIVED) (ProjectManagementPanel.tsx:97-124).

responsive.layout: Full-screen overlay (fixed inset-0, p-3 md:p-6) containing a max-w-[1500px], max-h-[94vh] flex-col panel: header, scrollable body (xl two-column: context cards + map | nearby list + decision card), sticky footer.
phoneRisks: 375x812: the 520px ArcGIS map fills ~65% of the viewport inside a 94vh scroll region; touch pans the map instead of the dialog — a scroll trap between the context cards and the decision controls (ProjectAssociationMap.tsx:196; ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx:148).
Order on a single column is header → 4 stacked context cards → map → nearby list (own 288px scroll) → decision card; the primary button is 3-4 screens down (ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx:155-291).
Two 'Close' buttons plus 'Continue to triage' in the footer; footer stays visible (good) but header Close is redundant (ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx:145,301).
Nested scroll regions: dialog body, nearby list, map — three competing gesture targets.
tabletRisks: 768-1279px: still single column (xl breakpoint), so map and list are stacked; 4 context cards fit at md (ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx:155,157).
1024px landscape: dialog is 1024-48px wide but still stacked; a lot of vertical scrolling for the decision card.
desktopNotes: At xl+ the map (1.7fr) and decision column (min 360px) sit side by side; primary button, selected-project summary and list all visible without scrolling on a 1080p display.
Dialog has role=dialog and aria-modal but no focus trap, no initial focus, and no Escape handler (ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx:135).

painPoints.issue: Dead code: never mounted; the live EventGroupAssociationDialog duplicates this flow for Event Groups, so two ~300-line association dialogs and two ArcGIS map components coexist.
painPoints.evidence: grep: ProjectAssociationDialog only defined at web/src/features/projects/ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx:34; live counterpart mounted at web/src/features/incidents/IncidentDecisionDialogs.tsx:73

painPoints.issue: Modal accessibility: no focus trap, no autofocus, no Escape-to-close; background remains tabbable.
Static 'Classification: Unclassified / Set after field assessment' card is identical for every incident — noise occupying one of four context slots.
Coordinates shown to 6 decimal places; not actionable and hard to scan.
Vocabulary drift: generated title says 'Route 1 · PM 12 · County Project' while location labels say 'R1 · PM 12'; note field is 'Coordinator note' here but 'Lifecycle note' in the management panel.
Duplicate Close buttons (header and footer).
Fixed 520px map height regardless of viewport; on phones the map alone exceeds 60% of the screen.
Radius select has no visible label (only the panel heading nearby).

strengths: Map + ranked list with distance and incident counts gives the coordinator two coordinated ways to pick a Project; selection syncs both (ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx:177-185,216-239).
Primary button label changes with state ('Project already assigned', 'Create Project and associate'), and it is disabled when nothing would change (ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx:132,284-287).
Sensible auto-mode: existing Project preselected, first nearby preselected, or Create new when nothing is nearby (ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx:59-69).
Prefilled generated title reduces typing for the create path (ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx:23-32,69).
Sticky footer explains the gate ('A Project association is required before triage can advance this incident.') and keeps Continue to triage always reachable (ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx:296-311).
Legend row under the map with the same three symbols used on the map (ProjectAssociationMap.tsx:197-201).

crossCutting: Dead legacy code: web/src/pages/ProjectsPage.tsx, web/src/pages/ProjectDetailPage.tsx, web/src/features/projects/ProjectManagementPanel.tsx, ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx, ProjectAssociationMap.tsx and ProjectDetailMap.tsx are imported by nothing routed (grep across web/src; App.tsx:77-78 only redirects /projects and /projects/:id). Only projectTypes.ts remains live, imported by web/src/features/missionCenter/MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:10 and MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:24-25 — Mission Center file names still say 'Project' while the UI says 'Event Group'.

Parallel type/helper duplication: eventGroupTypes.ts and projectTypes.ts are field-for-field copies (event_group_key vs project_uuid); eventGroupLocationLabel (eventGroupTypes.ts:71-79) and projectLocationLabel (projectTypes.ts:98-106) are identical; eventGroupStatusLabel and projectStatusLabel are identical (eventGroupTypes.ts:81-85; projectTypes.ts:108-112).

formatDate is re-declared in four files with two different output formats: Intl 'Sep 5, 2026, 3:04 PM' (EventGroupsPage.tsx:9-15, EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:12-18) vs toLocaleString with seconds (ProjectsPage.tsx:9-13, ProjectDetailPage.tsx:15-19). eventLabel is duplicated (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:20-22, ProjectDetailPage.tsx:21-23). inputClass is duplicated (ProjectManagementPanel.tsx:11, ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx:21).

Two status badges for the same OPEN/CLOSED/ARCHIVED enum: EventGroupStatusBadge (EventGroupsPage.tsx:17-24, 11px, py-0.5, 45%/10% mixes) and StatusBadge (ProjectsPage.tsx:15-22, xs, py-1, 42%/9% and 35%/8% mixes); ProjectDetailPage.tsx:98 renders a third, uncoloured pill. EventGroupStatusBadge is exported from a page module and imported by another page (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:10) rather than living in features/eventGroups or ui.

No shared Button component; at least five hand-rolled variants in this area: toolbar 'rounded-md border px-3 py-2 text-sm font-medium' (EventGroupsPage.tsx:73, EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:29), chip 'rounded border px-2 py-1 text-[11px]' (EventGroupsPage.tsx:91, EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:129-131), 'rounded-md px-3 py-1.5 text-xs' (ProjectsPage.tsx:115), 'rounded-md px-2.5 py-1.5 text-xs' (ProjectDetailPage.tsx:125), brand primary 'bg-[var(--brand)] text-white' (ProjectManagementPanel.tsx:120,151; ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx:285,306) and a green 'success' lifecycle button (ProjectManagementPanel.tsx:107,172).

Navigation semantics diverge: live Event Group pages use <Link> (EventGroupsPage.tsx:86,91; EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:77-78,121,129-131) while legacy Projects pages use <button onClick={navigate}> for the same purposes (ProjectsPage.tsx:106,115; ProjectDetailPage.tsx:82,125), which breaks open-in-new-tab and link semantics.

Vocabulary inconsistencies: 'active' (open_incident_count) vs status 'Open' vs incident 'In progress'; 'Last activity' (list/detail) vs 'Latest incident activity' (ProjectDetailPage.tsx:105); table header 'Links' (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:112) vs 'Action' (EventGroupsPage.tsx:80, ProjectDetailPage.tsx:117); location abbreviations 'D7 · R1 · PM 12.3' are never expanded on screen while the legacy generated title spells out 'Route N'; 'Coordinator note' vs 'Lifecycle note'; the permanent event_group_key exists in the API (eventGroupTypes.ts:27) but the UI only ever shows the numeric 'Event Group #id' while insisting incidents must have a 'permanent incident key' (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:103).

Hard-coded fetch limits with no pagination or truncation notice: 500 groups (EventGroupsPage.tsx:38), 500 projects (ProjectsPage.tsx:36), 1000 assessments fetched wholesale on every Event Group detail load/refresh to derive assessment/submission links (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:54).

Responsive vocabulary is thin: only md and xl prefixes are used across the whole area (EventGroupsPage.tsx:63; EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:75,107; ProjectsPage.tsx:61-70; ProjectDetailPage.tsx:79,93,112; ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx:135,155,157). No sm/lg/2xl. Every table relies on overflow-x-auto with no mobile card layout; ArcGIS maps use fixed inline pixel heights (420px ProjectDetailMap.tsx:24; 520px ProjectAssociationMap.tsx:28) that become scroll traps on touch; action chips are ~22px tall (text-[11px] py-1).

Accessibility gaps: search inputs and selects have no accessible label beyond placeholder (EventGroupsPage.tsx:65-66; ProjectsPage.tsx:77-78; ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx:195); load-error banners lack role=alert except the integrity banner (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:82 vs 102); tables have no caption; link text relies on hover colour only (EventGroupsPage.tsx:86; EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:121); the legacy modal has role=dialog but no focus trap or Escape handling (ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx:135); maps expose only an aria-label with the list as the sole keyboard path (ProjectDetailMap.tsx:107; ProjectAssociationMap.tsx:196); tooltip on a disabled button (ProjectManagementPanel.tsx:106).

Read-only-by-design record pages (AppShell.tsx:64-70 IA comment) mean the live Event Group detail carries no lifecycle/edit actions, whereas the dead legacy Project detail carried Edit/Close/Reopen with a well-designed inline confirmation (ProjectManagementPanel.tsx:97-175). Confirm My Work covers group closure or port that panel; otherwise coordinators have no UI to close an Event Group.

The live Event Group pages dropped three things the legacy Project detail had: an inline incident map with legend (ProjectDetailMap.tsx), a per-incident classification column with provenance copy (ProjectDetailPage.tsx:25-36,114), and KPI cards on the list (ProjectsPage.tsx:70-74). The first is replaced by link-outs to Mission Center; the other two have no replacement.

API fields returned but never rendered: EventGroupSummary.event_group_key, source, anchor_*/centroid_* coordinates, created_by_user_id, closed_at, closed_by_user_id (eventGroupTypes.ts:27,31-35,41,46-47); EventGroupIncidentSummary.incident_type, approved_at, approved_by_user_id (eventGroupTypes.ts:8-11); EventGroupEvent.metadata (eventGroupTypes.ts:61). Closed-by/closed-at in particular would be cheap, useful secondary information on CLOSED groups.

Inline-style colour usage bypasses tokens in two places: the broken-row tint (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:119) and the legend swatches using Tailwind palette colours bg-red-600 / bg-slate-500 / bg-amber-500 instead of --bad/--muted/--warn tokens (ProjectDetailMap.tsx:110-111; ProjectAssociationMap.tsx:198-199).
